label: Silk Road innovations
summary: The plural of the game concept Silk Road Innovation (innovations that travel west along the Silk Road).
details: In a text, `[silk_road_innovations|E]` shows "Silk Road Innovations" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the game rule for starting Silk Road innovations.

label: Silk Road
summary: The game concept Silk Road: not a single road but a network of routes that carries gold, goods and ideas between distant lands.
details: Access to it gives gold bonuses depending on its level and may unlock exotic innovations. In a text, `[silk_road_situation|E]` shows "Silk Road" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sin
summary: The game concept Sin: traits that a rite considers sinful.
details: Characters with such traits get opinion penalties from everyone who sees them as sinful, even of another rite, and lose piety every month if their own rite counts them as sins. Which traits are sins varies by rite. In a text, `[sin|E]` shows "Sin" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sin weight
summary: The game concept Sin Weight: how strongly a rite counts a trait as a sin, set by the rite's core tenets, doctrines and religion.
details: The traits with the highest sin weight in a rite become that rite's sins. In a text, `[sin_weight|E]` shows "Sin Weight" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in trait descriptions with the weight's value. The concept's description is shared with Virtue Weight.

label: Sinful
summary: Another name of the game concept Sin (traits a rite considers sinful), shown as the word "Sinful".
details: In a text, `[sinful|E]` shows "Sinful" linked to the Sin explanation; vanilla uses it often, for example in decisions that swap a sinful trait for a virtuous one.

label: Duel
summary: Another name of the game concept Single Combat (two characters fighting to the death or to first blood), shown as the word "Duel".
details: In a text, `[single_combat_duel|E]` shows "Duel" linked to the Single Combat explanation; vanilla uses it as a verb too ("allowing you to duel criminals").

label: Duels
summary: The plural of the game concept Single Combat, shown as "Duels".
details: In a text, `[single_combat_duel_plural|E]` shows "Duels" linked to the Single Combat explanation; vanilla uses it in AI personality texts.

label: Single combat
summary: The game concept Single Combat: two characters fighting each other, to the death or to first blood.
details: Each round both pick one of several randomly rolled options, which depend on their prowess and traits, until one lands a solid blow; many options raise their success chance and injury risk. In a text, `[single_combat_fight|E]` shows "Single Combat" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Single combats
summary: The plural of the game concept Single Combat (two characters fighting to the death or to first blood).
details: In a text, `[single_combat_fight_plural|E]` shows "Single Combats" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in a trial-by-combat text.

label: Sudden death
summary: A name linked to the game concept Single Combat, shown as "Sudden Death".
details: In a text, `[single_combat_fight_sudden_death|E]` shows "Sudden Death" linked to the Single Combat explanation. Vanilla uses it in single combat results as a reason why someone won or lost.

label: Risk of injury
summary: The game concept Risk of Injury: the chance a fighter in single combat hurts themselves, by opening their guard or with their own weapon.
details: It builds up as the fight goes on, so longer duels make self-injury easier. Its counterpart is the likelihood of success. In a text, `[single_combat_injury_chance|E]` shows "Risk of Injury" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Injure
summary: Another name of the game concept Risk of Injury (a duelist's chance of hurting themselves), shown as the verb "Injure".
details: In a text, `[single_combat_injury_chance_injure|E]` shows "Injure" linked to the Risk of Injury explanation; vanilla uses it in single combat tooltips ("easier for my foe to injure themselves").

label: Injury risk
summary: Another name of the game concept Risk of Injury (a duelist's chance of hurting themselves), shown as "Injury Risk".
details: In a text, `[single_combat_injury_chance_injury_risk|E]` shows "Injury Risk" linked to the Risk of Injury explanation; vanilla uses it in single combat results ("due to my Injury Risk score").

label: Duel edge bonus
summary: The game concept Duel Edge Bonus: a short-lived advantage in a duel, for example from terrain or traits, that raises prowess for the current bout.
details: It is lost right after the bout. Its opposite is the Duel Edge Penalty. In a text, `[single_combat_prowess_bonus|E]` shows "Duel Edge Bonus" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Duel edge penalty
summary: The game concept Duel Edge Penalty: a short-lived disadvantage in a duel, often from being badly hurt or intimidated, that lowers prowess for the current bout.
details: The lost prowess comes back right after the bout. Its opposite is the Duel Edge Bonus. In a text, `[single_combat_prowess_malus|E]` shows "Duel Edge Penalty" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Likelihood of success
summary: The game concept Likelihood of Success: how well a fighter is doing in a single combat.
details: To win, a fighter must get it well above the opponent's; as rounds pass, a smaller lead is enough. Its counterpart is the risk of injury. In a text, `[single_combat_success_chance|E]` shows "Likelihood of Success" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Duel success
summary: Another name of the game concept Likelihood of Success (how well a fighter is doing in single combat), shown as "Duel Success".
details: In a text, `[single_combat_success_chance_skill|E]` shows "Duel Success" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in single combat results ("due to their Duel Success score").

label: Sins
summary: The plural of the game concept Sin (traits a rite considers sinful).
details: In a text, `[sins|E]` shows "Sins" linked to the Sin explanation; vanilla uses it in concept texts on sin weight and on how sins affect rulers.

label: Situation
summary: The game concept Situation: a medium- to long-term affair involving the characters of a geographic region, moving through different phases.
details: In a text, `[situation|E]` shows "Situation" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it widely, for example when a situation moves to a new phase.

label: Situation catalyst
summary: The game concept Situation Catalyst: an event in a situation that can make it move from one phase to another.
details: The situation window lists which catalysts matter in each phase. In a text, `[situation_catalyst|E]` shows "Situation Catalyst" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in Christian Church decisions and interactions.

label: Catalyst
summary: Another name of the game concept Situation Catalyst (an event that can move a situation to another phase), shown as "Catalyst".
details: In a text, `[situation_catalyst_catalyst|E]` shows "Catalyst" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the Silk Road's list of latest catalysts.

label: Catalysts
summary: The plural of the game concept Situation Catalyst, shown as "Catalysts".
details: In a text, `[situation_catalyst_catalysts|E]` shows "Catalysts" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in Dynastic Cycle texts.

label: Dynastic cycle era
summary: The game concept Dynastic Cycle Era: the social and political state of China's dynastic cycle.
details: The eras fall into stable, unstable and chaos types. In a text, `[situation_dynastic_cycle_phase|E]` shows "Dynastic Cycle Era" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in government and legitimacy texts.

label: Dynastic cycle eras
summary: The plural of the game concept Dynastic Cycle Era (the social and political state of China's dynastic cycle).
details: In a text, `[situation_dynastic_cycle_phases|E]` shows "Dynastic Cycle Eras" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Participant group
summary: The game concept Participant Group: a set of characters in a situation who share the same effects in each phase.
details: In a text, `[situation_participant_group|E]` shows "Participant Group" linked to the concept's explanation. The debug lines given write `[situation_participant_group.GetName]`, which uses a scope of the same name, not this concept.

label: Participant groups
summary: The plural of the game concept Participant Group (characters in a situation who share the same effects per phase).
details: In a text, `[situation_participant_groups|E]` shows "Participant Groups" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the Christian Church window and disaster texts.

label: Situation phase
summary: The game concept Situation Phase: one stage of a situation, with its own modifiers and conditions for the characters involved.
details: Some phases begin when certain conditions are met, others simply follow over time. In a text, `[situation_phase|E]` shows "Situation Phase" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Situation phases
summary: The plural of the game concept Situation Phase (a stage of a situation with its own effects).
details: In a text, `[situation_phases|E]` shows "Situation Phases" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Exceptional bounty
summary: The game concept Exceptional Bounty: a phase of the Silk Road for good times, when great treasures and profits can be had and ideas and innovations spread widest.
details: In a text, `[situation_silk_road_phase_exceptional_bounty|E]` shows "Exceptional Bounty" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in building and Silk Road texts that push a region toward this phase.

label: Hardship
summary: The game concept Hardship: a phase of the Silk Road for bad times, when war or calamity bring trade to a standstill and neither money nor ideas move.
details: In a text, `[situation_silk_road_phase_hardship|E]` shows "Hardship" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in Silk Road texts that push regions toward this phase.

label: Steady trading
summary: The game concept Steady Trading: a phase of the Silk Road for ordinary times, when business goes on as usual and profits are reliable if not the highest.
details: In a text, `[situation_silk_road_phase_steady_trading|E]` shows "Steady Trading" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in Silk Road texts that push regions toward this phase.

label: Situations
summary: The plural of the game concept Situation (a long-running affair in a region that moves through phases).
details: In a text, `[situation_situations|E]` shows "Situations" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the concept texts on regions and catalysts.

label: Situation region
summary: The game concept Situation Region: one of the regions a situation can have, each moving through its phases on its own.
details: In a text, `[situation_sub_region|E]` shows "Situation Region" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in Silk Road building and effect texts.

label: Situation regions
summary: The plural of the game concept Situation Region (a region of a situation with its own phases).
details: In a text, `[situation_sub_regions|E]` shows "Situation Regions" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in Silk Road texts about downstream regions.

label: Christian Church chapter
summary: The game concept The Christian Church Chapter: a phase of the Christian Church situation, called a chapter.
details: There are seven chapters, grouped into four chapter types. In a text, `[situation_the_christian_church_phase|E]` shows "The Christian Church Chapter" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Christian Church chapters
summary: The plural of the game concept The Christian Church Chapter (a phase of the Christian Church situation).
details: In a text, `[situation_the_christian_church_phases|E]` shows "The Christian Church Chapters" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the concept text on chapter types.

label: Skill
summary: Another name of the game concept Skills: a character's ability values, which measure how good they are at different things.
details: The five main skills are diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue and learning. In a text, `[skill|E]` shows "Skill" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it very often.

label: Skill challenges
summary: The game concept Skill Challenges: moments in an event where a character can use a skill to change the outcome.
details: The higher the skill or skills involved, the likelier a good outcome. In a text, `[skill_challenges|E]` shows "Skill Challenges" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the survey activity.

label: Challenges
summary: Another name of the game concept Skill Challenges (event moments decided by a skill), shown as just "Challenges".
details: In a text, `[skill_challenges_no_prefix|E]` shows "Challenges" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Skills
summary: The game concept Skills: a character's ability values, which measure how good they are at different things.
details: The five main skills are diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue and learning. In a text, `[skills|E]` shows "Skills" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Skirmisher
summary: Another name of the game concept Skirmishers: lightly armed men-at-arms skilled at harassing the enemy.
details: They usually counter heavy infantry and are countered by archers. In a text, `[skirmisher|E]` shows "Skirmisher" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Skirmishers
summary: The game concept Skirmishers: lightly armed men-at-arms skilled at harassing the enemy.
details: Each kind is different, but they generally counter heavy infantry and are countered by archers. In a text, `[skirmishers|E]` shows "Skirmishers" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Soldier
summary: Another name of the game concept Soldiers: the troops of a regiment or army, whether levies, men-at-arms or knights.
details: In a text, `[soldier|E]` shows "Soldier" linked to the Soldiers explanation; vanilla uses it in the concept texts on damage and toughness.

label: Soldier icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Soldiers (the troops of a regiment or army).
details: Its text is only the soldier icon (`@soldier_icon!`). Vanilla writes it as the levies icon and, with `|E`, as a linked icon in front of levy counts.

label: Soldiers
summary: The game concept Soldiers: a collective word for the troops in a regiment or army, whether levies, men-at-arms or knights.
details: Having the most soldiers helps win battles and sieges. In a text, `[soldiers|E]` shows "Soldiers" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it often, for example in combat tooltips.

label: Son of Heaven
summary: The game concept Son of Heaven: the hegemon of China and top liege of the celestial government.
details: The Son of Heaven has the Mandate of Heaven as a special form of legitimacy and a participant group of their own. In a text, `[son_of_heaven|E]` shows "Son of Heaven" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Son of Heaven's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Son of Heaven (the hegemon of China).
details: In a text, `[son_of_heaven_possessive|E]` shows "Son of Heaven's" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in movement and catalyst texts.

label: Sōryō
summary: Another name of the game concept Sōryō Government: a feudal government unique to Japan, of local lords who rule their provinces as their own fiefs.
details: In a text, `[soryo|E]` shows "Sōryō" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in texts about house blocs and their wars.

label: Sōryō government
summary: The game concept Sōryō Government: a feudal government unique to Japan, of local lords who pushed aside the central government and rule provinces as their own fiefs.
details: Its characters do not use influence, but noble family heads keep their family manor and house aspiration. In a text, `[soryo_government|E]` shows "Sōryō Government" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sōryō icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Sōryō Government (Japan's feudal government).
details: Its text is only the government's icon (`@government_type_soryo!`); vanilla writes `[soryo_i|E]` as a linked icon, for example in front of the Sōryō ruler opinion modifier.

label: Soulmate
summary: The game concept Soulmate: a relation of deep romantic love, stronger than being lovers.
details: A character can have only one soulmate. In a text, `[soulmate|E]` shows "Soulmate" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Soulmate's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Soulmate (a relation of deep romantic love).
details: In a text, `[soulmate_possessive|E]` shows "Soulmate's" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Soulmates
summary: The plural of the game concept Soulmate (a relation of deep romantic love).
details: In a text, `[soulmates|E]` shows "Soulmates" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in effect texts where two characters become soulmates.

label: Soulmates'
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Soulmate.
details: In a text, `[soulmates_possessive|E]` shows "Soulmates'" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Spearmen
summary: The game concept Spearmen: men-at-arms who fight on foot with polearms.
details: They generally counter heavy and light cavalry, are countered by heavy infantry, and are often strong in hills and mountains. In a text, `[spearmen|E]` shows "Spearmen" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Special building
summary: The game concept Special Building: a unique, usually very powerful building found in a few set places, such as ancient wonders, great cathedrals and notable mines.
details: Some exist at the start of the game, others must be built. In a text, `[special_building|E]` shows "Special Building" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it for special building slots.

label: Special buildings
summary: The plural of the game concept Special Building (a unique building in a set place).
details: In a text, `[special_buildings|E]` shows "Special Buildings" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla notes that they use their own slots.

label: Special guest
summary: The game concept Special Guest: a guest of honour at a grand activity, such as the honoured guest of a feast or the champion at a tournament.
details: Special guests are more likely to accept the invitation, and the activity waits for them to arrive. In a text, `[special_guest|E]` shows "Special Guest" linked to the concept's explanation. Lines such as `[special_guest.GetFirstName]` use a saved scope of the same name, not this concept.

label: Special guests
summary: The plural of the game concept Special Guest (a guest of honour at a grand activity).
details: In a text, `[special_guests|E]` shows "Special Guests" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Special soldiers
summary: The game concept Special Soldiers: troops not raised from a holding but gained through events, such as retinues, hordes or rebel peasants.
details: They normally cost no upkeep and do not reinforce. In a text, `[special_troops|E]` shows "Special Soldiers" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in effect texts that destroy such troops.

label: Spectate
summary: Another name of the game concept Spectator (a character who watches a contest instead of competing), shown as the verb "Spectate".
details: In a text, `[spectate|E]` shows "Spectate" linked to the Spectator explanation; vanilla uses it in the concept's own description.

label: Spectating
summary: Another name of the game concept Spectator (a character who watches a contest instead of competing), shown as "Spectating".
details: In a text, `[spectating|E]` shows "Spectating" linked to the Spectator explanation. No vanilla text uses it.

label: Spectator
summary: The game concept Spectator: a character who watches a contest because they may not compete in it.
details: Possible contestants can also choose to opt out instead of competing. In a text, `[spectator|E]` shows "Spectator" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Spectators
summary: The plural of the game concept Spectator (a character who watches a contest instead of competing).
details: In a text, `[spectators|E]` shows "Spectators" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in a contest concept text.

label: Offer spiritual counsel
summary: The game concept Offer Spiritual Counsel: an interaction in which a cleric gives a character spiritual fulfillment in exchange for a hook.
details: In a text, `[spiritual_counsel_interaction|E]` shows the interaction's name, "Offer Spiritual Counsel", linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in a tenet that lets learned secular rulers use it.

label: Spiritual fulfillment
summary: The game concept Spiritual Fulfillment: how much at peace a character feels with their faith.
details: Its baseline comes from the character's traits and whether their faith sees them as sinful or virtuous. It rises or falls with behaviour the faith approves or not, and personal tenets can offset it. In a text, `[spiritual_fulfillment|E]` shows "Spiritual Fulfillment" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Spiritual fulfillment icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Spiritual Fulfillment (how much at peace a character feels with their faith).
details: Its text is only the icon (`@spiritual_fulfillment_icon!`). Vanilla uses it as the prefix of spiritual fulfillment modifiers and next to sin and virtue trait values.

label: Spiritual fulfillment level
summary: The game concept Spiritual Fulfillment Level: one of the bands a character's spiritual fulfillment is split into, each with its own effects.
details: Low levels make life harder and sinful acts cheaper; high levels make devotion easier and open new religious options. In a text, `[spiritual_fulfillment_level|E]` shows "Spiritual Fulfillment Level" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Spiritual fulfillment levels
summary: The plural of the game concept Spiritual Fulfillment Level (a band of spiritual fulfillment with its own effects).
details: In a text, `[spiritual_fulfillment_levels|E]` shows "Spiritual Fulfillment Levels" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it outside the concept's own description.

label: Spiritual head of faith
summary: The game concept Spiritual Head of Faith: a theocratic head of faith who does not need to hold land, though they can, such as the Pope.
details: Such heads of faith usually have interactions like granting claims or gold, and call great holy wars when the faith's doctrines allow them. In a text, `[spiritual_head_of_faith|E]` shows "Spiritual Head of Faith" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Sponsor
summary: The game concept Sponsor: a ruler who pays for the project of an inspired character.
details: In a text, `[sponsor|E]` shows "Sponsor" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in inspiration texts and achievements.

label: Sponsored
summary: Another name of the game concept Sponsor (a ruler who funds an inspired character's project), shown as "Sponsored".
details: In a text, `[sponsored|E]` shows "Sponsored" linked to the Sponsor explanation; vanilla uses it in a cultural innovation about artifacts from sponsored inspirations.

label: Spouse
summary: The game concept Spouse: a character's husband or wife, gained through marriage.
details: A spouse or concubine is needed for legitimate children and heirs, marriage or betrothal is the only way to form an alliance, and the main spouse sits on the council. In a text, `[spouse|E]` shows "Spouse" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it very often.

label: Spouse's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Spouse (a character's husband or wife).
details: In a text, `[spouse_possessive|E]` shows "Spouse's" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it for a spouse's house.

label: Spouses
summary: The plural of the game concept Spouse (a character's husband or wife).
details: In a text, `[spouses|E]` shows "Spouses" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Cultural spread
summary: Another name of the game concept Cultural Spread: contact with other cultures that know an innovation makes a culture discover it faster.
details: Among the eligible cultures, the one with the highest cultural acceptance is picked to spread its progress. In a text, `[spread|E]` shows "Spread" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in the culture window.

label: Spymaster
summary: The game concept Spymaster: the councillor in charge of intrigue and intelligence.
details: A disloyal spymaster can easily hide, or take part in, a murder scheme against you and your close family. In a text, `[spymaster|E]` shows "Spymaster" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: State rite
summary: Another name of the game concept State Rite: the rite an administrative government supports, tied to the title rather than to a character.
details: In a text, `[state_faith|E]` shows the same words as the State Rite concept, linked to its explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: State rite
summary: The game concept State Rite: the rite an administrative government supports, attached to the title and not to any one character.
details: Characters in the realm are easy to convert to it and very hard to convert away from it. Only the ruler of the administrative realm can change it, while governors may convert to it freely. In a text, `[state_rite|E]` shows "State Rite" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Station
summary: Another name of the game concept Stationed Regiment (men-at-arms placed in a holding for bonuses), shown as the verb "Station".
details: In a text, `[station|E]` shows "Station" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in an important-action text about stationing men-at-arms.

label: Station regiment
summary: Another name of the game concept Stationed Regiment, shown as "Station Regiment".
details: In a text, `[station_regiment|E]` shows "Station Regiment" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it on the button to pick a men-at-arms location.

label: Stationed
summary: Another name of the game concept Stationed Regiment (men-at-arms placed in a holding for bonuses), shown as "Stationed".
details: In a text, `[stationed|E]` shows "Stationed" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it often, for example in building bonuses for stationed men-at-arms.

label: Stationed holding
summary: A name linked to the game concept Stationed Regiment, shown as "Stationed Holding": the holding where men-at-arms are stationed.
details: In a text, `[stationed_holding|E]` shows "Stationed Holding" linked to the Stationed Regiment explanation; vanilla uses it in the regiment window.

label: Stationed regiment
summary: The game concept Stationed Regiment: a men-at-arms regiment placed in a holding, which makes it more effective.
details: Buildings can raise the bonus, usually for one or two types of men-at-arms. Stationing is possible at any time except during war and in some other cases. In a text, `[stationed_regiment|E]` shows "Stationed Regiment" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Meritocratic khanate
summary: The game concept Meritocratic Khanate: a bureaucratic government grown out of a nomadic one, similar to the celestial and meritocratic governments.
details: The liege appoints civil and military governors, while keeping tributaries, enforcing obedience and having a higher maximum dread. In a text, `[steppe_admin|E]` shows "Meritocratic Khanate" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Meritocratic khanate icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Meritocratic Khanate (a bureaucratic government grown from a nomadic one).
details: Its text is only the government's icon (`@government_type_steppe_admin!`); vanilla writes `[steppe_admin_i|E]` as a linked icon, for example in front of the ruler opinion modifier.

label: Steppe season
summary: The game concept Steppe Season: the current climate of the Great Steppe, which affects county fertility and the actions open to the rulers involved.
details: Each region has its own season, and nomad rulers may want to move to regions with good seasons. In a text, `[steppe_season|E]` shows "Steppe Season" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Steppe seasons
summary: The plural of the game concept Steppe Season (the current climate of a Great Steppe region).
details: In a text, `[steppe_seasons|E]` shows "Steppe Seasons" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Steward
summary: The game concept Steward: the councillor in charge of running the domain, such as taxes, culture and development.
details: In a text, `[steward|E]` shows "Steward" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Stewards
summary: The plural of the game concept Steward (the councillor who runs the domain).
details: In a text, `[stewards|E]` shows "Stewards" linked to the concept's explanation; vanilla uses it in doctrine texts on who may hold council posts.

label: Stewardship
summary: Another name of the game concept Stewardship Skill: the skill that helps rulers manage their domains.
details: It raises taxes directly, which makes it useful for every ruler; its lifestyle is the stewardship lifestyle. In a text, `[stewardship|E]` shows "Stewardship" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Stewardship skill
summary: The icon form of the game concept Stewardship Skill (the skill that helps a ruler manage their domain and raises their taxes).
details: `[stewardship_i]` shows the stewardship skill icon instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it right before `[stewardship_skill|E]` or `[stewardship|E]` in council task texts about the kurultai member's skill.

label: Stewardship lifestyle
summary: The game concept Stewardship Lifestyle: the lifestyle for characters who want a better domain, happier liege and vassals, or a lot of gold.
details: In a text, `[stewardship_lifestyle|E]` shows "Stewardship Lifestyle" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the effect texts that tell how much stewardship lifestyle experience a character gains.

label: Stewardship lifestyle
summary: The icon form of the game concept Stewardship Lifestyle (the lifestyle for improving one's domain, pleasing liege and vassals, or gaining gold).
details: `[stewardship_lifestyle_i]` shows the stewardship lifestyle icon instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it at the start of a bookmark character's description.

label: Stewardship skill
summary: The game concept Stewardship Skill: the skill that helps a ruler manage their domain and directly raises their taxes.
details: In a text, `[stewardship_skill|E]` shows "Stewardship Skill" linked to the concept's explanation. Its lifestyle is the stewardship lifestyle. Vanilla uses it in council task texts that show how a councillor's stewardship adds to the task.

label: Stewardship contract
summary: The game concept Stewardship Contract: a task contract for adventurers that usually means doing a census or putting up buildings.
details: In a text, `[stewardship_task_contract|E]` shows "Stewardship Contract" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Stewardship contract
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Stewardship Contract (a task contract that usually means a census or building work).
details: In a text, `[stewardship_task_contract_possessive|E]` shows "Stewardship Contract's" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Stewardship contract
summary: The plural form of the game concept Stewardship Contract (task contracts that usually mean a census or building work).
details: In a text, `[stewardship_task_contracts|E]` shows "Stewardship Contracts" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of a decision event that creates up to a number of such contracts on the map.

label: Stewardship contract
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Stewardship Contract (task contracts that usually mean a census or building work).
details: In a text, `[stewardship_task_contracts_possessive|E]` shows "Stewardship Contracts'" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Stockade
summary: The game concept Stockade: where a camp keeps its prisoners, the counterpart of a ruler's dungeon.
details: In a text, `[stockade|E]` shows "Stockade" linked to the concept's explanation. The concept shares its description with the dungeon: prisoners kept there gain stress and lose health, and may die of illness or suffer mental breaks. Vanilla's prisoner concept text says that in a camp all prisoners are kept in the stockade.

label: Stockade
summary: The plural form of the game concept Stockade (where a camp keeps its prisoners).
details: In a text, `[stockades|E]` shows "Stockades" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the plural form of a regional custom text that names the prison.

label: Tour stop
summary: Another name of the game concept Tour Stop: one stage of a royal tour, at which the liege attends a dinner, tours a vassal's grounds or enjoys a cultural festival.
details: In a text, `[stop|E]` shows "Stop" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in activity texts, for example that each stop of a tour lasts 2 months.

label: Tour stop
summary: The plural form of the game concept Tour Stop (the stages of a royal tour).
details: In a text, `[stops|E]` shows "Stops" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the travel planner, for the count of selected stops, and in the tour tutorial.

label: Story of El Cid
summary: The game concept for the bookmark story of Rodrigo Díaz, El Cid: optional story content in which he is cast aside by his liege, lives in exile and ends either back at court or taking Valencia.
details: In a text, `[story_content_el_cid|E]` shows "The Story of Rodrigo Díaz 'the Campeador'" linked to the concept's explanation. Its description calls the story style light and says the player can always opt out of story content. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Story of Hasan
summary: The game concept for the bookmark story of Hasan Sabbah: optional story content about religious fanaticism, converting counties away from their rulers and ending in a great religious uprising.
details: In a text, `[story_content_hasan|E]` shows "The Story of Hasan Sabbah" linked to the concept's explanation. Its description calls the story style moderate and says the player can always opt out of story content. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Story of Hereward
summary: The game concept for the bookmark story of Hereward the Wake: optional story content in which he returns from exile to fight Norman rule in England, ending with his death or his enemy's.
details: In a text, `[story_content_hereward|E]` shows "The Story of Hereweard 'the Wake'" linked to the concept's explanation. Its description calls the story style extensive: a special mechanic tracks England's resistance and scripted story events play. The player can always opt out. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Story of Jamukha
summary: The game concept for the bookmark story of Jamukha: optional story content in which he must choose between staying loyal to Temüjin and betraying him.
details: In a text, `[story_content_jamukha|E]` shows the concept's name linked to its explanation; in vanilla that name is built from Temüjin's bookmark name ("The Story of High Chieftain Temüjin"), the same as Temüjin's own story. Its description calls the story style light and says the player can always opt out. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Story of Temüjin
summary: The game concept for the bookmark story of Temüjin: optional story content about avenging his imprisoned spouse on a rival tribe and testing the loyalty of his friend Jamukha.
details: In a text, `[story_content_temujin|E]` shows "The Story of High Chieftain Temüjin" linked to the concept's explanation. Its description calls the story style light and says the player can always opt out. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Story of Wallada
summary: The game concept for the bookmark story of Wallada bint al-Mustakfi: optional story content in which she raises a unique poet trait by writing poetry and founding salons, improving a unique book along the way.
details: In a text, `[story_content_wallada|E]` shows "The Story of Wallada bint al-Mustakfi" linked to the concept's explanation. Its description calls the story style moderate and says she gets ways to keep playing although she is childless. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Story
summary: The game concept Story: a personal situation tied to a ruler, such as owning a dog or becoming a conqueror.
details: In a text, `[story_cycle|E]` shows "Story" linked to the concept's explanation. A story is built from parts such as key characters, titles or decisions. Vanilla uses it in the situation list ("not involved in a situation, struggle, or story") and in story endings.

label: Story
summary: The plural form of the game concept Story (personal situations tied to a ruler).
details: In a text, `[story_cycles|E]` shows "Stories" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the situation list window's header.

label: Governor
summary: The plural of strategos, another name of the game concept Governor: the main vassals a ruler with an administrative government appoints to run the realm's lands.
details: In a text, `[strategoi|E]` shows "Strategoi" linked to the Governor concept's explanation. A governor's title and its counties form a province, where governance issues can appear for them to solve. Vanilla uses it in a chariot race intent text and in a custom text for the plural.

label: Governor
summary: Another name of the game concept Governor: a main vassal appointed by a ruler with an administrative government to run part of the realm.
details: In a text, `[strategos|E]` shows "Strategos" linked to the Governor concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a custom text that gives the governor's name for a culture or government.

label: Request claim endorsement
summary: The game concept Request Claim Endorsement: an interaction that turns an unpressed claim into a pressed one with the backing of a fitting clergy (ecclesiastical or theocratic) ruler.
details: In a text, `[strengthen_claim_interaction|E]` shows "Request Claim Endorsement" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that give the interaction more acceptance.

label: Stress
summary: The game concept Stress: what a character builds up by acting against their personality traits.
details: In a text, `[stress|E]` shows "Stress" linked to the concept's explanation. Enough stress gives a stress level with harmful effects until the stress goes down; activities such as a hunt relieve it. Vanilla uses it very often, for example in decision tooltips ("gain stress") and feast amenity texts.

label: Stress
summary: The icon for critical stress gain, a form of the game concept Stress (what a character builds up by acting against their traits).
details: `[stress_critical_i]` shows the critical stress icon instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the Stress concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it before the amount in the effect texts for gaining critical stress.

label: Stress
summary: The icon for stress gain, a form of the game concept Stress (what a character builds up by acting against their traits).
details: `[stress_gain_i]` shows the stress gain icon instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the Stress concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it before the amount in the effect texts for gaining stress.

label: Stress
summary: The icon form of the game concept Stress (what a character builds up by acting against their traits).
details: `[stress_i]` shows the stress icon instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it before `[stress|E]` in activity and important action texts, and at the start of the name of an adventurer lifestyle action.

label: Stress level
summary: The game concept Stress Level: a level a character gains for every 100 stress, from 0 to 3.
details: In a text, `[stress_level|E]` shows "Stress Level" linked to the concept's explanation. Each level lowers fertility and health more, and from level 1 on the character can have mental breaks. Vanilla uses it in achievements and interaction requirements ("You need a higher stress level").

label: Stress level
summary: The plural form of the game concept Stress Level (the levels a character gains for every 100 stress).
details: In a text, `[stress_levels|E]` shows "Stress Levels" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the mental break concept text.

label: Stress
summary: Another name of the game concept Stress, shown as the words Stress Loss (stress is what a character builds up by acting against their traits).
details: In a text, `[stress_loss|E]` shows "Stress Loss" linked to the Stress concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in perk and travel effect texts about how much stress is lost.

label: Stress
summary: The icon for stress loss, a form of the game concept Stress (what a character builds up by acting against their traits).
details: `[stress_loss_i]` shows the stress loss icon instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the Stress concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it in court position and perk texts where stress goes down.

label: Stress level
summary: Another name of the game concept Stress Level, shown as the word Stressed (a level a character gains for every 100 stress).
details: In a text, `[stressed|E]` shows "Stressed" linked to the Stress Level concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for interactions only allowed while stressed, such as dueling criminals.

label: Strife
summary: The game concept Strife: an opinion penalty among fellow vassals when one of the liege's subjects acts against another vassal.
details: In a text, `[strife|E]` shows "Strife" linked to the concept's explanation. The description names a diarch using their diarch powers, and mandate events, as causes. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that warn of strife with peer vassals or say strife goes down.

label: Strife
summary: Another name of the game concept Strife, shown as the words Strife Opinion (an opinion penalty among fellow vassals).
details: In a text, `[strife_opinion|E]` shows "Strife Opinion" linked to the Strife concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Church centralization
summary: Another name of the game concept Church Centralization, shown as the words Strong Centralization (how far the Church has centralized its authority and money).
details: In a text, `[strong_centralization|E]` shows "Strong Centralization" linked to the Church Centralization concept's explanation. The stronger the centralization, the more income goes up the clerical hierarchy; strong is one of its three types. Vanilla uses it in a Christian Church text about the share of theocratic leases.

label: Strong hook
summary: The game concept Strong Hook: a very powerful hook on a character, for example one you have blackmailed.
details: In a text, `[strong_hook|E]` shows "Strong Hook" linked to the concept's explanation. It can do all a weak hook can and more, such as forcing the target to be an agent in a murder; the target cannot act hostile towards the holder. Using it does not spend it: it goes on a cooldown. Vanilla uses it often, in achievements, scheme and interaction texts.

label: Strong hook
summary: The icon form of the game concept Strong Hook (a very powerful hook on a character).
details: `[strong_hook_i]` shows the icon of an unspent strong hook instead of a word; with `|E` it is also linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes it before `[strong_hook|E]` in scheme and interaction texts, such as offering agents a strong hook.

label: Strong hook
summary: The plural form of the game concept Strong Hook (very powerful hooks on characters).
details: In a text, `[strong_hooks|E]` shows "Strong Hooks" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in achievements, the hook concept text and journey activity texts.

label: Strong vassal
summary: The game concept Strong Vassal: a vassal who comes close to or exceeds their liege in power and thinks less of them for it.
details: In a text, `[strong_vassal|E]` shows "Strong Vassal" linked to the concept's explanation. The vassal gets an opinion penalty towards the liege. Vanilla uses it as the name of that opinion reason.

label: Strong vassal
summary: The plural form of the game concept Strong Vassal (vassals who come close to or exceed their liege in power).
details: In a text, `[strong_vassals|E]` shows "Strong Vassals" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Struggle
summary: The game concept Struggle: a long conflict over a large region with many faiths and cultures, lasting decades or centuries.
details: In a text, `[struggle|E]` shows "Struggle" linked to the concept's explanation. Inside a struggle's region special rules and modifiers apply and change as it moves through its phases. Vanilla uses it often, for example in the effect text that starts a struggle.

label: Struggle catalyst
summary: The game concept Struggle Catalyst: a notable action that pushes a struggle's region towards a new phase.
details: In a text, `[struggle_catalyst|E]` shows "Struggle Catalyst" linked to the concept's explanation. Which actions count in which phase is listed in the struggle window. Vanilla uses it in messages that report a catalyst being triggered.

label: Struggle catalyst
summary: Another name of the game concept Struggle Catalyst, shown as the word Catalyst (a notable action that pushes a struggle towards a new phase).
details: In a text, `[struggle_catalyst_catalyst|E]` shows "Catalyst" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the names of the individual catalysts, such as "Yearly Drift Catalyst".

label: Struggle catalyst
summary: The plural form of the game concept Struggle Catalyst, shown as the word Catalysts.
details: In a text, `[struggle_catalyst_catalysts|E]` shows "Catalysts" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in other struggle concept texts.

label: Struggle clash
summary: The game concept Struggle Clash: a small local war in a struggle in which a ruler grabs land by conquering or vassalizing a target.
details: In a text, `[struggle_conquest|E]` shows "Struggle Clash" linked to the concept's explanation. Its prestige cost depends on the struggle's current phase. Vanilla uses it as the name of the struggle county casus belli.

label: Struggle clash
summary: Another name of the game concept Struggle Clash, shown as the word Clash (a small land-grabbing war in a struggle).
details: In a text, `[struggle_conquest_conquest|E]` shows "Clash" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the war name (an attacker's adjective, then Clash, against the defender).

label: Struggle clash
summary: The plural form of the game concept Struggle Clash, shown as the word Clashes.
details: In a text, `[struggle_conquest_conquests|E]` shows "Clashes" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Ending decision
summary: The game concept Ending Decision: a unique decision that ends a struggle, often only available in certain phases.
details: In a text, `[struggle_ending_decision|E]` shows "Ending Decision" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a struggle bonus name.

label: Ending decision
summary: The plural form of the game concept Ending Decision (unique decisions that end a struggle).
details: In a text, `[struggle_ending_decisions|E]` shows "Ending Decisions" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Interloper
summary: The game concept Interloper: a character caught up in a struggle but not fully involved in it.
details: In a text, `[struggle_interloper|E]` shows "Interloper" linked to the concept's explanation. An interloper's capital is in the struggle region, but they do not have both an involved faith and an involved culture; involved characters see them as troublesome outsiders. Vanilla uses it in list texts such as "Every Interloper ruler".

label: Interloper
summary: The plural form of the game concept Interloper (characters caught up in a struggle but not fully involved).
details: In a text, `[struggle_interloper_interlopers|E]` shows "Interlopers" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the struggle phase effects heading for interlopers.

label: Involved
summary: The game concept Involved: a character or county that the people of a struggle region see as a natural part of the struggle.
details: In a text, `[struggle_involved|E]` shows "Involved" linked to the concept's explanation. Involved characters get the full benefits of the struggle's phases and are the main ones to trigger catalysts. Vanilla uses it very often, for example in "Every Involved ruler".

label: Involved culture
summary: The game concept Involved Culture: a culture that is involved in a struggle, from its start or later as things change.
details: In a text, `[struggle_involved_culture|E]` shows "Involved Culture" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Involved culture
summary: The plural form of the game concept Involved Culture (cultures involved in a struggle).
details: In a text, `[struggle_involved_cultures|E]` shows "Involved Cultures" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a struggle tutorial text.

label: Involved faith
summary: The game concept Involved Faith: a faith that is involved in a struggle, from its start or later as things change.
details: In a text, `[struggle_involved_faith|E]` shows "Involved Faith" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Involved faith
summary: The plural form of the game concept Involved Faith (faiths involved in a struggle).
details: In a text, `[struggle_involved_faiths|E]` shows "Involved Faiths" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a struggle tutorial text.

label: Struggle large conquest
summary: The game concept Struggle Large Conquest: a major war won by the attacker that counts for some struggle catalysts.
details: In a text, `[struggle_large_conquest|E]` shows "Struggle Large Conquest" linked to the concept's explanation. Its description lists the casus belli that count, such as duchy conquest, invasion and major religious wars. Vanilla uses it in the catalyst for winning such a war against another involved ruler.

label: Concession
summary: The game concept Concession: the quiet ending of the Persian struggle, when both sides tire of the bloodshed.
details: In a text, `[struggle_persia_phase_concession|E]` shows "Concession" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an event option that activates a catalyst towards it.

label: Stabilization
summary: The game concept Stabilization: a phase of the Persian struggle in which the caliph still has respect and rebels are on the back foot.
details: In a text, `[struggle_persia_phase_stabilisation|E]` shows "Stabilization" linked to the concept's explanation. The struggle can slide from it into Unrest. Vanilla uses it in decision requirements ("the current struggle phase is Stabilization") and catalyst texts.
